note: City documents published after the workbook, and the sources that ballot.json cites beyond it. Sources here continue the workbook's numbering (S20 onwards). Every quote, here and in ballot.json, must appear on its page of source/excerpts/{source}.json (whitespace-normalized; page 1 for a web page). The build parses every number from its quote, so a number can't drift from its source. News excerpts keep only the paragraphs quoted.

salesTaxMeasure.quote: CITY ATTORNEY’S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE V

salesTaxRevenue.quote: The City estimates the tax will generate $9 to $10 million annually.

salesTaxRevenueCouncil.quote: the tax is estimated to generate approximately $9 million - $10 million annually

salesTaxTerm.quote: the tax would go into effect beginning April 1, 2027, and last until ended by the voters

salesTaxGeneral.quote: This would be a general tax, meaning the revenue from the tax would be placed into the General Fund and could be spent on any valid municipal purpose.

bondMeasure.quote: CITY ATTORNEY’S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE U

bondCost.quote: the average annual taxpayer costs over the projected 40 years that the bonds would be outstanding are approximately $22.14 per $100,000 of assessed property value; generating approximately $15,200,000 per year

bondPeak.quote: $35 per $100,000 of assessed value, which the City projects would begin to apply in 2040-41

bondAudit.quote: All expenditures would be subject to an audit by the City Auditor at least once every three years

adoption.quote: as contained in the City Manager’s FY27 & FY28 Proposed Biennial Budget, and as amended by subsequent Council action

adoptionGap.quote: The City projects General Fund structural deficits of $29.25 million in FY27 (after the allocation of one-time resources) and $29.53 million in FY28.

capitalNeedGrowth.quote: (1) Capital & Maint. Needs are current estimates of unfunded needs. Needs are estimated to increase at a rate of 4% per year.

oneTimeDelay.quote: The City Manager has recommended utilizing one-time funds during Fiscal Year 2027 to delay the closure of Fire Station 4 until after the results of the Sales and Use Tax measure are disclosed in November 2026.

capitalProgram.note: FY27 and FY28 columns of 'Capital program by funding source - all funds' (p.170): every fund row, tied out to its fund type's Total row. The General Fund's CIP fund is broken down by program category on pp.172-173 ('… Total' rows), tied out to the p.170 row and to that table's Grand Total.
